archetype.name: Gunslinger (in a run-first system)
archetype.definition: A big-armed, mobile passer who has always carried a high interception count and takes a lot of sacks hunting for plays downfield, now asked to work inside the most run-heavy offense in the league.

report.headline: Sacks, picks and late-game collapses: a Herbert-plus-line problem, not just Herbert
report.take:
Herbert has never been a low-risk quarterback. He finished 58th of 62 in interceptions in 2021 and 60th of 63 last year. His pressure-to-sack rate has climbed from .171 as a rookie to .333 in 2024 and .297 in 2025. What carried that profile was efficiency: positive EPA every season, CPOE near or above zero, and real rushing value (498 yards last year, 2nd at the position). In 2026 the risk is still there and the efficiency is gone. His -0.223 EPA per dropback ranks 41st of 45, his 8 interceptions rank dead last, and the Chargers are 0-6.

Two things are driving it. The first is a sudden accuracy drop. His CPOE is 7.2 points below last season, yet his bad-throw rate is up only 1.1. That gap suggests the collapse isn't purely ball placement. It points just as much at what he's throwing into and to whom. Targets to TE Oronde Gadsden II have produced -0.523 EPA apiece, while McConkey, Harris and Johnston are all positive. The second is the environment. This offense passes 11.4 points below expectation (32nd), allows a hit rate of 0.205 (30th), and the sack rate has reached 10.4%. That puts him on a 17-game pace of 60 sacks and 23 interceptions. Some of the sack-taking is him, given the career trend, but a line now missing Joe Alt and Kayode Awosika makes it worse.

The numbers also hide where the damage happens. He's been almost functional when the game is out of hand, with -0.13 EPA when trailing by 9+ and a CPOE near zero. In one-score games he has posted -0.39 EPA on 118 plays. In close fourth quarters it's -1.155 per play, with 9 sacks and 2 picks on 28 plays, adding up to -32.3 EPA. Most of his season's damage sits in those few snaps. That is a mix of a one-dimensional offense being forced to pass when everyone knows it, a leaky line, and Herbert pressing.

The last three weeks were the worst stretch (-0.308 EPA per dropback, 12.4% sack rate). They also came against Seattle, Kansas City and Denver, now ranked 2nd, 3rd and 7th in defensive EPA. That context matters, but it doesn't excuse much. He wasn't good against Arizona, Las Vegas or Buffalo either. Expect better than this, because his history says he's a league-average-or-better passer. The ceiling stays capped by volume, protection and a thin receiver room until Alt and Harris are back.

strengths.title: Legs remain a real asset
strengths.body: Even in a broken season he ranks 6th at the position in rushing yards, and he's been running more lately, at 40 a game over the last three. Scrambles are mildly positive by EPA, which shows he can still salvage collapsed pockets. This is a career-long trait (2nd in rushing last year), so it should last.

strengths.title: Intermediate throws to wideouts work
strengths.body: The 10-to-19-yard window is the one depth where he's positive, at +0.032 EPA with a 48.9% success rate. His wideouts are all producing: McConkey at 0.66 EPA per target, Harris and Johnston both above 0.2. The arm and the reads are still there when he works outside to his receivers. The issue is how rarely the offense lets him do it.

strengths.title: Clean in the red zone
strengths.body: All five of his touchdown passes came inside the 20, with no interceptions and a CPOE right at average there. Red-zone EPA is still slightly negative, so call this ball security rather than dominance. It's a small sample.

concerns.title: Sacks are killing drives
concerns.body: A 10.4% sack rate ranks 40th of 45, and he's converting more than a third of pressures into sacks. That is consistent with his career drift (.333 in 2024), so part of it is him holding the ball for a big throw. A 30th-ranked team hit rate and two starting linemen out make it worse. It should ease when Alt returns but won't go away.

concerns.title: Turnovers on throws downfield
concerns.body: Seven of his eight interceptions have come on throws of 10+ air yards, with three on just 20 deep attempts that he completes 30% of the time. He has always thrown picks, but a 4.4% interception rate is well above his normal. Expect it to come down some, while staying a weakness of his game.

concerns.title: Collapses when games are close
concerns.body: In close fourth quarters he has added -32.3 EPA on 28 plays, with 9 sacks and a 14.3% success rate. A run-first offense that becomes predictable when it has to pass is part of it. So is pressing behind a weak line. Until this flips, losses will keep piling up regardless of how the first three quarters go.

trend.note: Each of the last three games got worse by EPA, bottoming out at -14 with no touchdowns at Kansas City. That stretch came against three top-seven defenses, but he was below average against the soft early schedule too.

nextGame.headline: A depleted Rams front meets a depleted Chargers line
nextGame.body:
The Rams are the softest pass rush he's seen. They rank 30th in hit rate and 28th in sack rate, and that was before the injuries. On paper it targets his biggest problem. They take away what he needs most, though: they're 1st in deep EPA allowed, stingiest of all against tight ends, and allow the 2nd-fewest yards to quarterbacks. A clean pocket may buy time without buying much downfield. The bye gives him 14 days of rest and the game is indoors.

Availability cuts both ways. Kobie Turner is expected to land on IR and Poona Ford is done for the year. Myles Garrett's practice window wasn't opened this week, so the interior rush should be thinner still. Trent McDuffie missed the last game with a groin injury. His listed return date has passed, so his status is worth checking. On the other side, Alt, Awosika and Tre Harris are all listed out with estimated returns on game day itself. McConkey is in the concussion protocol. If Harris and McConkey both sit, the targets shift toward Gadsden, whose -0.523 EPA per target is the worst on the team, against the league's best defense versus tight ends. With Davante Adams out for the Rams, this projects as a low-scoring, close game. That's exactly the script where he has struggled most.

keyMatchups.title: Weakened Rams rush vs his sacks
keyMatchups.body: The Rams rank near the bottom in both hit rate and sack rate and are now missing Turner and Ford, with Garrett not yet back. If the Chargers' patched line holds even moderately, this is his best chance all season at a single-digit sack rate.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots into the stingiest secondary
keyMatchups.body: The Rams allow the lowest deep EPA in the league, and his deep passing is already 30% completions with three picks. Patience to the intermediate area, his one positive zone, matters more than ever here.

keyMatchups.title: Tight end looks are a dead end
keyMatchups.body: Gadsden has been his most costly target, and the Rams rank 1st against TE1s by both EPA and points over average. If his receivers are out, he can't afford to lean on the tight end.

nextGame.watch: Whether Harris and McConkey suit up. With them, the clean pocket the Rams' injuries should allow can produce; without them, it likely won't.

restOfSeason.body:
Some of this will regress toward his career. A 4.4% interception rate and a CPOE more than seven points below last year are outliers for a passer with six straight seasons of positive EPA. The return of Alt and Harris, both estimated for November 1, would address the two biggest environmental drags. What won't change is the structure. Harbaugh's offense passes far less than situation predicts, so the volume ceiling stays low, and his sack tendency is a multi-year trait. Expect him to settle in as a below-average-to-average efficiency passer with useful rushing, not a return to his 2021 form.

Realistically that looks like 185 to 225 passing yards and about one touchdown pass a game, with interceptions dropping toward one or fewer and sacks still elevated. His rushing at 25 to 38 yards a game is the steadiest part of his fantasy floor.
swingFactors: Joe Alt's return at left tackle
Health of Tre Harris and Ladd McConkey
Whether Harbaugh opens up the pass rate when trailing

confidence.note: Six games against a tough recent schedule and heavy injuries, set against a long, stable career baseline.
